extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for Inventiones Mathematicae (research mathematicians submitting to the journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission of a research manuscript to the journal Inventiones Mathematicae, including formatting, ethical declarations, artwork/supplementary material preparation, authorship rules, and post-acceptance steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channel and picking an editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be submitted in electronic form as a PDF file attached to an electronic message sent to one of the editors. An author should pick the editor scientifically closest to the topic of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt, e-mail the submission to one of the managing editors (specific names given). Email addresses are provided on the journal site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript originality and simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission implies the work described has not been published before and is not under consideration for publication elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work must be original; simultaneous submission to multiple journals is not permitted. Publisher not legally responsible for compensation claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval by co-authors and institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication must have been approved by all co-authors and by the responsible authorities at the institute where the work was carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approval may be tacit or explicit and is required before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for reused material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors wishing to include figures, tables, or text passages already published elsewhere must obtain permission from the copyright owner(s) and include evidence of such permission when submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material submitted without evidence of permission will be assumed to originate from the authors. Be aware some publishers may not grant electronic rights for free and Springer will not refund permission costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide editable source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should preferably be submitted in the original file format and in PDF; ensure you provide all relevant editable source files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to submit source files may cause unnecessary delays in review and production. For LaTeX submissions include all style files and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be submitted in electronic form as a ps or pdf file attached to an electronic message; LaTeX and Word files are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer LaTeX using Springer Nature LaTeX template; include original source and a PDF of compiled output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Title page must contain title, author names, affiliations (institution, (department), city, (state), country), and clear indication and active e-mail address of the corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If available, include 16-digit ORCID for authors. For temporarily unaffiliated authors capture city and country; e-mail only if specifically requested. Acknowledgments should be placed in a separate section on the title page and funding organisations written in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an abstract of 150 to 250 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should not contain undefined abbreviations or unspecified references. (Additional trial registration requirements for life sciences when applicable.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and Declarations required
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a 'Statements and Declarations' section for items such as Competing Interests and other relevant declarations; submissions missing relevant declarations will be returned as incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are required to disclose financial or non-financial interests related to the work. Examples and wording templates are provided in other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification codes (MSC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an appropriate number of Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSC is used by reviewing databases; see AMS MSC list for codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the decimal system of headings with no more than three levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent hierarchical numbering throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations should be defined at first mention and used consistently thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid undefined abbreviations in abstract and main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes can give additional information, may include citation of a reference; they should not consist solely of a reference citation and should never include bibliographic details of a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to text numbered consecutively; footnotes to tables indicated by superscript letters (or asterisks for statistical data). Footnotes to title/authors are not given reference symbols. Always use footnotes instead of endnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement and funder naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Place acknowledgments of people, grants, funds, etc. in a separate section on the title page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the names of funding organisations in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical notation and scientific style
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard mathematical notation should be used: italic for single letters (variables/constants), roman/upright for numerals, operators, and commonly defined functions (cos, det, e, exp, lim, log, max, min, sin, tan, d), bold for vectors/tensors/matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow common discipline conventions for symbol styling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference citations in the text should be identified by numbers in square brackets (e.g., [3], [1-3]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place citations according to examples provided in the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list content and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference list should include only works cited in the text and that have been published or accepted for publication; personal communications and unpublished works should be mentioned only in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should be numbered consecutively. If available, always include DOIs as full DOI links. Use standard journal name abbreviations per ISSN LTWA; if unsure, use full journal title. Examples provided for journal article, article by DOI, book, book chapter, online document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables numbered using Arabic numerals and cited in text in consecutive numerical order. Each table should have a caption explaining the components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify previously published material by giving original source as a reference at the end of the table caption. Footnotes to tables indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks) and included beneath table body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats and electronic submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all figures electronically and indicate what graphics program was used; for vector graphics preferred format is EPS; for halftones use TIFF format. MSOffice files are also acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name figure files with 'Fig' and the figure number, e.g., Fig1.eps. Vector graphics containing fonts must have fonts embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line art requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Line art: black and white graphics with no shading should not use faint lines/lettering; all lines should be at least 0.1 mm (0.3 pt) wide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scanned line drawings and line drawings in bitmap format should have minimum resolution of 1200 dpi. Embed fonts in vector graphics containing fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone and combination artwork resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Halftone (photographs, drawings with fine shading) should have minimum resolution of 300 dpi. Combination artwork should have minimum resolution of 600 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If magnification is used in photographs, indicate using scale bars within figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color art guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Color art is free of charge for online publication. If black-and-white will be shown in print, ensure the main information is visible when converted to black-and-white; do not refer to color in captions if printed B/W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit color illustrations as RGB (8 bits per channel). Check xerographic copy to ensure distinctions remain apparent in B/W.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure lettering fonts and sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: For figure lettering use Helvetica or Arial (sans serif). Keep lettering consistently sized throughout final-sized artwork (about 2–3 mm, 8–12 pt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variance of type size within an illustration should be minimal; avoid effects such as shading, outline letters, etc. Do not include titles/captions within illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering, parts and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures numbered using Arabic numerals and cited in text in consecutive numerical order. Figure parts should be denoted by lowercase letters (a, b, c, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appendix contains figures, continue consecutive numbering of the main text (do not use A1, A2 etc.). Figures in online appendices (SI) should be numbered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure captions format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure should have a concise caption describing accurately what the figure depicts. Captions begin with the term 'Fig.' in bold, followed by the figure number in bold; no punctuation after the number or at the end of the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include captions in the text file, not in the figure file. Identify all elements found in the figure and acknowledge previously published material with a reference at the end of the caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure placement and sizing in manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be submitted within the body of the text unless file size causes upload problems; size figures to fit column width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dimensions specified for large-sized journals (84 mm for double-column, 174 mm single-column width; max height 234 mm), for small-sized journals 119 mm wide and not higher than 195 mm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure accessibility so people of all abilities/disabilities can access figure content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide descriptive captions usable by screen readers; use patterns instead of or in addition to colors; any figure lettering must have contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI images policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must check Springer’s policy on generative AI images and ensure work adheres to those principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific linked policy when using generative AI to create images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information (SI) accepted formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer accepts electronic multimedia and other supplementary files (animations, movies, audio) and other file types for online publication alongside an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submitting research datasets as SI, read the journal’s Research data policy. Encourage archiving data in repositories. Supply SI in standard formats and include article title, journal name, author names, affiliation and corresponding author email in each file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary files technical constraints and naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep larger-sized files in mind for download times; maximum video file size 2 GB, minimum video duration 1 sec; supported video formats listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text and presentations: submit as PDF; spreadsheets as .csv or .xlsx; specialized formats (.pdb, .wrl, .nb, .tex) are allowed. Multiple files can be zipped. Name SI files consecutively (e.g., ESM_3.mpg).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing and captioning Supplementary Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Text must make specific mention of SI similar to figures/tables; refer to SI as 'Online Resource' and cite (e.g., Online Resource 3). Each SI file should have a concise caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SI will be published as received without conversion/editing. Number and name files consecutively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information accessibility and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Make SI accessible: include descriptive captions; video files must not contain flashing more than three times per second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with accessibility and safety requirements for SI content. Check generative AI image policy for SI as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibilities and COPE compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal follows COPE guidelines and expects authors to refrain from misrepresenting research results and to uphold integrity of the scientific record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow rules of good scientific practice listed (no multiple submissions, originality, no salami-slicing, honest data presentation, adherence to discipline-specific data processing rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and image manipulation prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Results should be presented clearly and honestly without fabrication, falsification or inappropriate data manipulation (including image manipulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to discipline-specific rules for acquiring, selecting and processing data. Journal may investigate suspected misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No data, text, or theories by others should be presented as the authors' own; proper acknowledgement must be given for copied or paraphrased material and permissions secured for copyrighted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal may use software to screen for plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for use of software/questionnaires/scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should ensure they have permissions for use of software, questionnaires/(web) surveys and scales in their studies, if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain necessary licensing or permission prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate citation and avoidance of excessive self-citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and non-research articles must cite appropriate and relevant literature; excessive or inappropriate self-citation or coordinated self-citation is strongly discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite literature that supports claims and avoid gaming citation metrics via self-citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding defamatory or untrue statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should avoid untrue statements about an entity or descriptions that could be personal attacks or allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims about individuals/companies are supported and not defamatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-use and potentially harmful research identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that may be misapplied to pose a threat to public health or national security must be clearly identified in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify dual-use concerns (e.g., biological agents, vaccine immunity disruption, weaponization) so editors and reviewers can assess risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship correctness at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly advised to ensure the author group, the Corresponding Author, and the order of authors are correct at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding/deleting authors during revision is generally not permitted; changes should be explained and are at the Editor-in-Chief's discretion. Changes cannot be made after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of raw data and documentation upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request authors should be prepared to send relevant documentation or data to verify validity of results (raw data, samples, records).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitive confidential or proprietary data is excluded from mandatory sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal investigation and possible sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspicion of misbehavior or fraud arises, the Journal/Publisher will investigate following COPE guidelines and may take measures depending on findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures include rejection, erratum/correction, expression of concern, retraction, informing author's institution, or noting suspected transgression in bibliographic records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to correct fundamental errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have an obligation to correct significant errors or inaccuracies once discovered and must contact the journal to explain how the error impacts the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision to issue correction or retraction depends on nature of error; retraction notes should transparently explain impacted parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting and excluding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest suitable reviewers and/or request exclusion of individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested reviewers must be independent and not connected to the work; recommend a mix from different countries/institutions. Provide institutional email for each suggested reviewer or other identity verification (personal homepage, publication record, researcher ID). The Journal may not use suggestions but they may facilitate peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended authorship criteria (adapted from ICMJE): (1) substantial contributions to conception/design, data acquisition/analysis/interpretation, or new software; (2) drafted or critically revised the work; (3) approved the version to be published; (4) agree to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher does not prescribe exact contribution types; adhere to field-specific authorship guidelines where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures and declarations required (funding/ethics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should include information on sources of funding, financial or non-financial interests, study-specific ethics committee approval for human/animal research, informed consent, and animal welfare statements as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on inclusion depend on scope of the journal and the article; include appropriate disclosures for public health implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data transparency expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should ensure that data, materials, and software/custom code support their published claims and comply with field standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may have individual policies on sharing research data in concordance with disciplinary norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and responsibilities of the Corresponding Author
rubrics_metrics.description: One author is assigned as Corresponding Author who acts on behalf of all co-authors and ensures questions related to accuracy/integrity are appropriately addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include ensuring all listed authors approved manuscript and order, managing communication between Journal and co-authors, providing transparency on reuse of material, and ensuring disclosures/declarations are included. Managing communication may be delegated to a Contact or Submitting Author if Corresponding Author is clearly indicated in manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contribution statements and CRediT taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher recommends including contribution statements specifying each author's contribution; examples provided including free-text and CRediT taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List contributions (Conceptualization, Methodology, Formal analysis, Writing, Funding acquisition, Resources, Supervision, etc.). For review articles include who had the idea, who did the literature search and data analysis, and who drafted/critically revised. For thesis-based articles recommend student listed as principal author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary affiliation for each author should be the institution where the majority of their work was done; if moved, current address may additionally be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses will not be updated after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to authorship policy after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes of authorship (adding/deleting authors, changing Corresponding Author or sequence) are not accepted after acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author names will be published exactly as they appear on the accepted submission; ensure names are present and correctly spelled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author identification and ORCID
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to use their ORCID ID when submitting or acquire one via submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing ORCID IDs improves author identification and is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of deceased or incapacitated authors
rubrics_metrics.description: If a co-author dies or is incapacitated during preparation/submission/review and co-authors feel inclusion is appropriate, co-authors should obtain approval from a legal representative such as a direct relative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow best practice for consent from legal representative before including the deceased/incapacitated author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship disputes resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: If an authorship dispute occurs during peer review or after acceptance/publication, the Journal will not adjudicate and authors will be asked to resolve the dispute themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors cannot resolve the dispute, the Journal may withdraw the manuscript or raise the issue with authors' institution(s) and follow institutional guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of communications with the Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should treat all communication with the Journal as confidential, including correspondence with Editors and reviewers' reports, unless explicit consent has been received to share information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality during peer review and editorial processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance production steps and proofing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance, article will be exported to Production for typesetting. Authors will receive emails to confirm affiliation, choose publishing model, arrange rights and payment, and a link to proofs once typesetting is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs should be used to check typesetting or conversion errors; substantial changes (new results, corrected values, title/authorship) are not allowed without Editor approval. Further changes after online publication only via Erratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article publishing agreement and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on journal ownership and policy, authors will either grant Publisher an exclusive licence or transfer copyright to the Publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Choice articles do not require transfer of copyright; authors publish under a Creative Commons license. Details of OA licences found in journal How to publish guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprints and color illustration charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Offprints can be ordered by the corresponding author. Online color publication is free; for print color authors may be expected to contribute towards extra costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will be informed about any charges during post-acceptance communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online First publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The article will be published online after receipt of corrected proofs; this is the official first publication citable with the DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After release of printed version the paper can also be cited by issue and page numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Choice (hybrid open access) and APCs
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Choice allows publishing open access in Springer Nature journals; Article Processing Charges (APCs) vary by journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include increased engagement and visibility; funding/support pages provided for help finding funding. APCs and OA license details are available on the journal's OA information pages.
